title: When the Confession Burns
premise: When a drowned man washes up in Hollow Creek wearing clothes cut from Juniper Hartwell's own closet, the small-town coroner realizes the corpse is wearing her past: the garments match, stitch for stitch, what she buried twelve years ago in an unsolved case she quietly closed. As Juniper reopens the file, she uncovers that the dead man was the true killer in a thirty-year-old murder for which an innocent woman was convicted, and that someone in town has been leaving her coded confessions for years. Torn between protecting the town's fragile peace and exposing the truth that will destroy her mentor and implicate her own family, Juniper follows the confession trail to its source. In the end, she testifies at the reopened trial, choosing truth over loyalty, and the real killer—her beloved retired sheriff father—is arrested as Juniper finally buries every grave by its honest name.
about_author: Isandro Dunmore is the pen name of a former rural court reporter who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. Known for procedurals steeped in grief and civic silence, Dunmore writes from a farmhouse where the nearest neighbor's porch light is a rumor.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A drowned stranger surfaces in Hollow Creek wearing clothes identical to hers; the wrongness of it unsettles her professional calm. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Grief
chapters.summary: Juniper catalogs the town's dead while introducing her meticulous filing system and her isolation. Flashback seed: a case she closed too fast twelve years ago. Beat: loneliness as armor.

chapters.title: Stolen Threads
chapters.summary: Juniper confirms the clothing was cut from fabric sold only to her late mother—a detail no outsider could know. Beat: the case turns personal.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Deputy Marisol Vega's POV. Vega interviews the sole witness, elderly Odette Crane, whose alibi contradicts records by exactly thirty years. Beat: first crack in the town's story.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Juniper rereads her old closed file on the Larkspur drowning and finds her own signature on a verdict she doesn't remember writing. Beat: self-doubt takes root.

chapters.title: Odette's Parlor
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. The old woman reveals she saw something thirty years ago but traded silence for protection. Beat: fear dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Father's Badge
chapters.summary: Retired Sheriff Amos Hartwell warns Juniper off the case over Sunday dinner, his concern curdling into control. Beat: love with strings attached.

chapters.title: The Coded Notes
chapters.summary: Juniper finds a slip of paper in the archive—her mother's handwriting, dated after her death, quoting scripture inverted into a threat. Beat: the dead are talking.

chapters.title: Trial Docket
chapters.summary: Vega's POV. The DA announces the Larkspur conviction will be vacated and retried, putting everyone's old alibis under oath again. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Juniper visits the cemetery she knows intimately and finds fresh flowers on the stranger's unmarked plot—someone mourns him. Beat: tenderness amid suspicion.

chapters.title: The Seamstress's Daughter
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, mother's era: a young seamstress sews three identical suits for three men who swore brotherhood. Beat: origins of the stolen clothes.

chapters.title: Alibi Thirty Years Deep
chapters.summary: Vega interviews townsfolk whose stories align too perfectly, word for word, like rehearsed testimony. Beat: conspiracy smells like choreography.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Juniper dives the creek site and recovers a locket engraved with her mother's initials. Beat: grief resurfacing literally.

chapters.title: Marisol's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vega's POV. She notices Juniper's name appearing in sealed records it should never touch. Beat: ally begins to suspect ally.

chapters.title: The Confession Letters
chapters.summary: A second note arrives at the morgue, addressed to 'the girl who files the dead,' detailing the night of the original murder. Beat: hunted by knowledge.

chapters.title: Brotherhood of Three
chapters.summary: Juniper identifies the three suit-owners: her father, the victim, and convicted man Dale Pruitt. Beat: the triangle closes.

chapters.title: Dale Pruitt's Cell
chapters.summary: Prison interview POV, Pruitt: he confesses he lied at trial to protect someone he loved. Beat: guilt without culpability.

chapters.title: Sunday Supper Trap
chapters.summary: Amos probes Juniper about the notes over dinner; she lies for the first time in her life. Beat: daughter against father, unspoken.

chapters.title: The Archive Fire
chapters.summary: Someone torches the records room; Juniper saves one box—her mother's sewing ledger. Beat: destruction narrows the truth.

chapters.title: Ledger of Sins
chapters.summary: The ledger shows a fourth suit, never delivered, sized for a boy. Beat: a hidden child enters the story.

chapters.title: Odette Breaks
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Pressured by the retrial, she admits she saw Amos at the creek that night—and that the fourth suit was for his secret son. Beat: the floor gives way.

chapters.title: Half-Brother
chapters.summary: Juniper traces the boy: grown now, living two counties away under another name—the drowned man himself. Beat: identity as inheritance.

chapters.title: Why He Came Home
chapters.summary: Vega's POV. The victim returned to claim his birthright and blackmail his father. Motive crystallizes. Beat: ambition meets blood.

chapters.title: The Clothes Were a Message
chapters.summary: Juniper realizes the killer dressed the body in her clothes to make her reopen the case—an invitation, not a frame. Beat: horror becomes purpose.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Diner
chapters.summary: Juniper confronts Amos publicly; he denies everything with a calm that terrifies her. Beat: the mask holds, barely.

chapters.title: Marisol Chooses
chapters.summary: Vega's POV. Ordered to surveil Juniper, she instead shares the sealed-file evidence. Beat: loyalty shifts from badge to truth.

chapters.title: Mother's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Hidden in the ledger, a letter reveals Juniper's mother knew of the affair and the child, and died before she could speak. Beat: inherited silence.

chapters.title: The Third Suit
chapters.summary: Juniper tracks the third suit-owner's descendants and learns Dale Pruitt took the fall for Amos out of love for Odette. Beat: sacrifice reframed.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Juniper stakes out the cemetery; a figure leaves flowers—Amos. She photographs him. Beat: proof and heartbreak in one frame.

chapters.title: Arrest Warrant Denied
chapters.summary: Vega's POV. The DA, an old friend of Amos, refuses the warrant. Beat: institutions protect their own.

chapters.title: Threats in the Filing Room
chapters.summary: Juniper is cornered and warned by an anonymous deputy; her files are ransacked. Beat: fear sharpens resolve.

chapters.title: Odette's Testimony
chapters.summary: Pretrial hearing: Odette recants thirty years of silence on the stand, naming Amos. Beat: courage at the end of a life.

chapters.title: Father and Daughter
chapters.summary: Amos comes to Juniper at midnight, neither confessing nor denying, asking only that she remember who raised her. Beat: love against duty, stated plainly.

chapters.title: The Missing Note
chapters.summary: Juniper decodes the final confession letter—it was written by her mother, planted to be found posthumously. Beat: the dead finish their sentence.

chapters.title: Trial Begins
chapters.summary: Courtroom POV, Juniper as witness. The defense paints her as a grieving, unstable daughter. Beat: truth on trial beside the guilty.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Juniper endures brutal questioning and produces the photograph, the ledger, and the locket. Beat: composure as weapon.

chapters.title: Verdict of Bones
chapters.summary: Forensic evidence ties Amos to the original drowning; the jury convicts on both counts. Beat: justice arrives cold and complete.

chapters.title: Visiting Hours
chapters.summary: Juniper visits her father in jail; they say goodbye without forgiveness. Beat: love surviving truth, diminished.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Juniper reburies the drowned man under his true name, with Odette and Pruitt's family present. Beat: names restored, graves honest.

chapters.title: When the Confession Burns
chapters.summary: Juniper burns her mother's confession letter at last, keeping only the memory, and opens a new, empty filing drawer. Beat: peace chosen, not found.
